utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I'm sorry we're late, but the earlier case had to continue a little longer to complete its business. We can now continue with the cross-examination of Mr. Adamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Adamovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As I said to you yesterday, the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your evidence continues to apply until your evidence is completed. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel. There were --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- a couple of things from yesterday I wanted to try and clear up with you. One of them had to do with the map excerpts that you would get from the Pristina Corps command for further distribution. Yesterday at page 25067 Judge Bonomy had asked you a question about whether you opened the envelopes that you got at the Pristina Corps, and you said: "No need for that." And then about 20 pages later at 25085 I had asked you how it was that Colonel Mijatovic knew to say that there were markings on the maps if you were receiving them in closed envelopes. And you explained that you saw the maps at the Pristina Corps during their preparation. My question is: When you were at the Pristina Corps did you have any input in the process of those maps being prepared before they went into the envelopes?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved in the drafting of the maps, if I may say so. There was a large map on which the units were shown movements of activities and so on and excerpts were made from that map, that is to say copies were made for the units that were to participate in that activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who physically put the map excerpts inside the envelopes, was that you or somebody from Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once I gave information about the units that were to participate I would go back to the staff; then later on when maps were completed, when excerpts were completed, they would invite me to come over and take them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it from that that somebody at Pristina Corps must have put them into the envelopes, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They had already been prepared. They were copied there later after the documents were produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So did Mijatovic know about the markings on the map because you told him about it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what markings you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, could you start your answer again, please, the interpreter did not catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether Mr. Mijatovic, and if so on which occasion, was able to see one of those maps since there were a number of actions and one would come to an end and another one would begin subsequently, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: A related question I have to the maps is yesterday I think at page 25073 you told us that the officers in the field from both the MUP and the VJ had daily contact, and we understood that the VJ commanders in the field were receiving their copies of the map excerpts. Wouldn't it have been just as simple for the VJ commanders to provide copies of the map excerpts to their MUP colleagues in the field rather than having them distributed through you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why this was done in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you just following up about the Joint Command. You mentioned you hadn't seen any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, I hope this isn't in addition to what you had planned for today because your 20 minutes is rigid.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you decide on your priorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mentioned having heard the word Joint Command. On the 5th of November, 1998, there was a meeting at the ministry staff in Pristina where President Milutinovic spoke and you're listed as attending that meeting. I will tell you that in that meeting he spoke of a meeting that had occurred a few days before and he said: "With regard to the Yugoslav Army and police everything will stay the same as it has been up until now, a Joint Command, VJ units will not withdraw, and police forces have only been reduced by the number already withdrawn." Do you recall hearing President Milutinovic mention the Joint Command at that meeting you attended in November 1998?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to say that you said that I had heard for the first time the word on the 5th of November; however --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to see where was it recorded that the witness said that he heard about the Joint Command for the first time on the 5th of November from Milutinovic. Where was it that the witness said that? If Mr. Hannis could please point us in the right direction I would be really grateful. Please check your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I did not say that he heard it for the first time at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's how it was translated to us, that you said that he had heard this term Joint Command for the first time. This is how it was translated to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not there in English, Mr. Fila --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see, but that's what the witness is hearing. He hears the interpretation into Serbian and that's how he's replying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you've clarified it and the witness now knows that he doesn't need to deal with that. He can now go directly to the question. Do you recall hearing President Milutinovic mention the Joint Command at the meeting you attended on the 5th of November, 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember whether he mentioned it, I can't remember details from that period of time. If that's what it says in the minutes then perhaps he did utter that, but I cannot claim that he did say that because I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 51 of your statement you tell us that Minister Stojiljkovic always had an extremely intolerant attitude to Sreten Lukic and did not hesitate to show it. Can you give us an example of this intolerant attitude that the minister had toward General Lukic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps one of the example was the fact that he was not appointed chief of secretariat, which would have been a normal course in the professional development of an officer. I think he was major-general at the time, and a colonel was appointed to the top position of the secretariat in Belgrade rather than him, a colonel who had occupied a much lower position prior to that. That was an illogical thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is that the only example you have?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember that example well, since I was employed at that secretariat myself. I wasn't trying to remember any other examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, your statement is a very broad statement that the minister always had an extremely intolerant attitude, so it would help to have another few examples.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't see that I used the term always -- oh, no, no, no, I see it here, yes, always.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you can't think of another example, I --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't think of one because it's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me move on. I have limited time. Let's have a look at Exhibit 1D680. I don't know if you might have seen this in the course of your preparation for testifying. It's a draft of a letter from Minister Stojiljkovic concerning a proposed promotion of General Lukic dated the 11th of May, 1999. Did you have a chance to see this prior to your coming here to testify?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If you'll look at the last paragraph above the signature, the English translation says: "In the past year Lukic has excelled in successful command and control of the MUP units engaged in the prevention of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. The highly positive results achieved in this field in the past period which are largely owed to Major-General Lukic are the best recommendation for promoting him." That doesn't seem to show an intolerant attitude of the minister towards General Lukic, does it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this example one can see perhaps that views or positions changed. We saw the previous example.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, you said he always had an intolerant attitude, so your statement's not correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I analysed it on the basis of this example, that I am well familiar with and it was enough for me to make my conclusions. I don't know whether my conclusions are correct or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And having read this now, does that change your mind?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was customary to have these promotions in our service. For example, officers would be promoted when they met certain requirements, having spent sufficient time in the lower rank and having done certain things, and it is on the basis of that context that I made my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me move to the last topic I want to cover with you and show you Exhibit P1064. This is a document dated the 28th of July, 1998, from Petar Ilic, chief of the defence administration, to defence departments. The subject is: Instructions for the defence of inhabited areas. The first paragraph says: "The Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija has issued instructions for the defence of inhabited areas ..." And my question relates to the second paragraph. It says: "In addition to the resubordination of conscripts from SMO units," which I believe is Federal Ministry of Defence units, "formed and mobilised by defence departments and sections to the MUP. These instructions focus on the engagement of the civil protection." You were aware, were you not, that federal defence units had been resubordinated to the MUP in the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this documented for the first time. I don't quite understand it since I had no contact and I had no information. When it comes to contacts with police and these activities concerning civilian -- civil protection and the Ministry of Defence, I simply don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I realized yesterday that we showed you a portion of a meeting from the 29th of July, 1998, that you attended where General Lukic spoke and said: "We're also arming citizens in towns and plans for defending towns have been drawn up." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I now want to show you a related exhibit to this cover letter, P2086, please. This is a lengthy document so I think it will help if I can hand you a hard copy with the help from the usher. And I would tell you I believe this is the attachment to that cover letter we just looked at. These are the instructions for the defence of inhabited places, and the first item I would have you look at - and it's on page 2 for you near the bottom, page 2 of the English - the instructions are intended for staffs responsible for commanding and controlling the defence of inhabited areas. And it says: "Given the different organizational and establishment structures of police units that defend towns and the purpose and capabilities of individual towns, the provisions of these instructions must be flexibly applied." Did you have no dealings with these defence plans that General Lukic talked about being drawn up at the end of July 1998?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had nothing to do with these plans. This is the first time that I see such a document. I don't know whether it was intended for that period of time or some future period of time. I simply don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If you could go to page 4 in your B/C/S version, and it's page 3 of the English. I'd like you to look at item number 2, which is entitled: "Forces for the defence of towns and their purpose." The first paragraph says: "In the specific conditions, the forces for the defence of cities and other inhabited areas are the MUP units, which unify all the forces in the inhabited area and organize, lead, and perform combat operations. They change their composition depending on the size and significance of the town." That's how it worked, wasn't it? MUP was responsible for leading the defence of inhabited areas, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is really not clear to me. I don't understand it, given that we know how the police forces functioned and I see here that combat activities are mentioned here as well. This is not something that the police does, at least not these units, the way I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it's simply not clear to me what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would you go to the next page of your document, and I'm continuing on the bottom of page 3 at the very bottom it says: "MUP reserve units in the cities also include members of civil protection and monitoring and reporting systems. The civil protection as an element of the MUP reserve composition operates primarily in the municipality." And then I skip a sentence and I'm on page 4 of the English: "Under the current conditions the civil protection units are not activated, but they are part of the unified system of the MUP reserve and they participate in combat operations during defence against attacks by terrorist forces." You didn't know that that's how the defence of towns was supposed to be accomplished in July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You'll need to -- I'm afraid, Mr. Adamovic, you'll need to start that answer again, please. There was a microphone problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to my information, civil protection even before 1998 and after 1998 was never part of the MUP, that's what I know. MUP had a reserve police force and there is a well-established procedure as to how that is done when it comes to reserve police force, both in Kosovo and outside of Kosovo. This is why I find it so difficult to interpret this document because it is not clear to me, I can't give you my position regarding it, because what I know from that field is simply different. I question, or rather, I can't question this document because somebody drafted it, but I just can't explain the text of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, who's the author of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the attachment that goes with the cover letter from Petar Ilic in Exhibit P1064. He was the chief of the defence administration, and we saw in that letter that conscripts from the Ministry of Defence were resubordinated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, and who was P1064 issued to?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is from Petar Ilic and it's going to the defence department sections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who are they?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: They're under the Ministry of Defence administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I know my 20 minutes are up, Your Honour, but I'd like to finish this topic, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll be as quick as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sir, could you go to page 9 of your document. I'm looking for item 5 which is entitled: "Commanding," and it's found on page 7 of the English. And I have a question about my English translation, so if you could read the first sentence under item number 5 for me I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Command and control is an activity undertaken by the staff which organizes the defence of the town. The commander of the unit organizing the defence is a police officer and he commands the forces that are engaged. The commander is responsible for executing the tasks assigned to them."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the English translation says: "Command and contrast." I think control makes more sense. I can submit it for -- this is a revised translation from CLSS. I can submit it or with agreement of the parties maybe we can all agree right now that that should be "control."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's no challenge to the interpretation today so we'll accept the translation that we've just heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the next paragraph, sir, says: "The staff functionally ties together and unites all the defence structures (the VJ reserve, the MUP, the CZ," civil protection, "enterprises and citizens) as 'the MUP reserve.'" So according to this it seems that in the defence of towns the commander is going to be a police officer and all those defence structures in the town include the VJ reserve, the MUP, the civil protection, enterprises, and citizens. You weren't aware that that's how the defence of towns was being organized?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this does not correspond to what was done on the ground. As far as I know there is no organ of this type in charge of the police in Kosovo. I know that the secretariats carried out the same tasks just like before 1998, so I don't know what this document is, whether it was somebody's wishful thinking or what. In practice this is not how it functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We know you disagree with the document. Can you please -- thank you. One last item I want to ask you about, if you could go to item number 7, I'm not sure what page that is in the B/C/S, page number 8 in the English, and that item is headed: "Fighting with sabotage and other special terrorist groups." Do you find that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you go to the very end of that item, the last paragraph above item number 8. I want to ask you about a comment there. We have to go to page 9 of the English now and I think we probably have to go to the next page in the B/C/S in e-court. The third line in that last paragraph says: "Destruction is attempted whenever possible, before they enter into an action. Achieving surprise is an important condition in the combat against these forces and operations are undertaken swiftly, boldly, and decisively, with the engagement of the population and other defence forces." Sir, this seems consistent with what we saw in some of the joint activity orders of VJ and MUP in anti-terrorist operations where it talks about using the armed non-Siptar population. And one of the meetings that you attended, you were present when Captain Pesic talked about some almost 60.000 people being armed in conjunction with the reserve police offices. Isn't that part of the overall defence plan, was to include not only the regular VJ and MUP forces and their reserve forces but the population, basically the non-Siptar population, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, we never discussed these things at the staff. Whether this is some sort of a plan from the previous period of time that was just copied down, that's just not clear to me. I am not familiar with this plan and I don't think that it is consistent with the situation on the ground because it mentions all structures, companies, enterprises, civilians, police, which is a very wide spectrum.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the last thing I have in conjunction with this is another document, P1135, if I can hand you a copy, there's one paragraph I want to ask you about. This is from the 14th of July, 1998, it's a regular operative report from the military district command in Pristina, item number 14 is: "Main task." It says: "Providing expert assistance to the MUP organs in preparing Serbian villages for defence. Conducting the training of citizens titled weapons and target practice and tactical training titled defence of populated areas." Were you not aware that the military district command was assisting the MUP in preparing Serbian villages for defence, particularly tactical training called defence of populated areas? You didn't know about that either?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that. What I knew is what I said earlier on, that a certain number of members of the reserve force of the military and the MUP had had weapons issued to them. So I haven't dealt with this subject and I'm unfamiliar with these documents. But - how should I put this? - the army carries out training. This was written by military officers. I don't know. I simply don't understand these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think you've answered my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have just one matter I want to ask you about, Mr. Adamovic. Who was it during your time at the staff who commanded OPGs?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: OPGs involved members of special police units from the secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija, that is to say that there were eight companies. Every secretariat had one respectively, Pristina had two companies, and within these companies there were say ten members in the OPGs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who commanded them when they were operating as an OPG?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were within companies. I was not out in the field so I don't know whether the plan was changed or not, but that means if there is ten from Djakovica, ten from Kosovska Mitrovica, and so on and so forth, then they were in those companies, yes, in those companies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And never brought together as an elite group?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I am not abreast of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, just a short one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Adamovic.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's just deal with what cropped up today regarding resubordination of units of the civilian protection to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please call up P1064.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see this document? The Prosecutor showed it to you as well.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that you had never seen this document. I would like to ask you about the organ sending this document. Is it a republican or a federal organ?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says it's federal, that's what's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the organ of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Republican.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was this letter sent to? Can you see at the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or rather, my question is: Does this document reflect whether it was ever sent to anyone in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to this document, document P2086 was shown to you so I'd like to have that called up in e-court as well, please. I need the last page, please. The first one will do as well. Let's see the first one first -- oh, now we have the last one. We're looking at the last page. Can it be seen whether this document was signed or stamped by anyone?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If page 13, the one on the screen, is the last one then there is nothing on it, nothing of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let us deal with the items that the prosecutor dealt with. Could we please have page 4 in B/C/S, 2(a), units and tasks of the civilian protection in the reporting and observation system, page 4, so I guess we need page 5 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the fifth page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to have page 4 displayed to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page with number 4 in B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have it now, page 4 of the document with a number 4. Could you please read paragraphs 1 and 2 for us. What are the tasks of the civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "1. General purpose CZ units: Administer first aid, rescue people from ruins, extinguish initial and smaller fires, clear barricades, organize the washing of streets, and so on."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Specialised units of the CZ perform larger-scale and professionally more complex tasks and rescues: Rescue from ruins (they can be construction, road, and fire-fighting units), administering first aid, destroying unexploded ordnance, clearing the terrain, maintaining order, and so on. They are organized in the same way as civil protection units for general purposes."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please read on. Could we have the next paragraph as well.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "This means that after undertaking combat operations these units are engaged in the implementation of these tasks without a special order (activation in case of imminent threat of war)."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This last sentence that you read out to us, does it show whether they were activated in July 1998 which is the date that we have on this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this shows that at that time they could not have been activated and that this document is probably on the basis of documents that are done in advance, and it depends what period this refers to. Perhaps it was first written many years ago and then it's just copied time and again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time when you were in Kosovo and Metohija - and we have seen what the tasks of these units are - have you ever heard of these civil protection units being subordinated to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of that, right here and now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for this document it was suggested to you by my colleague Mr. Hannis that the police commanded the reserve units of the Army of Yugoslavia in urban areas. While you were in Kosovo and Metohija did you ever have occasion to see the police commanding reserve units of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that quite simply that is not possible in terms of the establishment we have in our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That will do as far as this subject is concerned. I would just like to go back quickly to a document that my colleague Mr. Ackerman showed you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please call up in e-court 6D716.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I made a mistake. Maybe it wasn't Mr. Ackerman, but that's what I've written down here. At any rate, the document was shown to you. And we need the last page of this document. This is a document that says in its heading that it was issued by the MUP command. I'm going to ask you about the initials at the end of the document on the last page. Do you see them?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out the first initials?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MDJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Think about this a bit, on the MUP staff while you were on the MUP staff was there a person there with those initials, MDJ?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you remember whether in the Pristina Corps there was a man with the initials MDJ?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's too late now, but I think this was a leading question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, I was asleep at that point I'm afraid, Mr. Cepic. It was indeed, Mr. Lukic. Please be careful with your leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know how else I could put this question. If he knows somebody in Pristina of course with these initials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why not ask him if he knows of anyone elsewhere with such initials or in any other organization with such initials or in some other position with such initials. Do you want me to go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, at the time while you were in Pristina, how many people did you know with these initials and please tell us the names of the persons whose initials were MDJ?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember Colonel Milan Djakovic. I can try to remember whether there is someone else I know. Quite simply, right this moment I cannot remember whether I knew anyone else with these initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Adamovic. Thank you for having come and testified. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, that completes your evidence. Thank you for coming here to give evidence. You may now leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, who is your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next witness is Mr. Nebojsa Bogunovic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bogunovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud the document now shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You'll now be examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Bogunovic. Your statement is going to be shown to you now so could you please have a look at it. Mr. Bogunovic, do you recognise the statement that is before you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Before me is the statement that I gave to you as Defence counsel, and it is authentic, it reflects my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is your signature on this statement?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you were to testify today would you answer the same questions in the same way?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I could add or take away anything from what this statement contains.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could Mr. Bogunovic's statement be admitted into evidence as 6D1614.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all we have for you at this point in time. Now probably some of my colleagues from the Defence will have some questions for you and then the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Bogunovic.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In order to move on faster and to make it easier I would like to call up in e-court document 6D798. You're going to see it on the screen now and I'm going to ask you about that.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I still don't have anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It will come up. Sir, Mr. Bogunovic, you did not attend this meeting, but the chiefs of secretariats attended it. Do you know that this meeting was held on the 22nd of July, 1998, in the staff of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can see that my superior, Colonel Adamovic, attended the meeting. I suppose that this is authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Upon his return from the meeting did he perhaps hold a meeting with you to brief you about the meeting that he had attended?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Whenever my superior went anywhere, upon his return he would always hold a meeting with us, his subordinates, and he would inform us about what had happened at that meeting and what our tasks were.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Upon his return from this particular meeting did he mention to you that one of the two generals that you see there, one is Obrad and the other one is Rodja, mentioned that some kind of a Joint Command was established for Kosovo and Metohija comprising civilians or noncivilians or anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: This is the first time I encounter this term, Joint Command, except in 1981 when there existed a Joint Command at the level of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: During that time you were in Djakovica when this meeting was held if I understood it correctly, right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: This is the time when I was in the territory of the Djakovica SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And then at some point later you were transferred to the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP where Mr. Cvetic was the chief?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: In November I was transferred pursuant to the decision of the chief of the sector, General Djordjevic, to Kosovska Mitrovica, where my superior was Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: During your stay with Mr. Cvetic while you served together with Mr. Cvetic, did Mr. Cvetic mention to you that there was some sort of a Joint Command mentioned at this meeting or did he tell you anything about the existence of this Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Given that I came to a new area that was not familiar to me, Cvetic informed me with the tasks, with my tasks, and with the situation on the ground in the territory of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP. Once again, I never heard this term nor did I ever see a document mentioning combined command.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Or Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: During your service did you see somebody interfering in the MUP chain of command?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, I received orders from my officers, in this case from Colonel Adamovic and Colonel Cvetic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: From my superior officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I see based on your statement that you are familiar with what Mr. Cvetic said in his statement about policemen and so on, and I'm not going to go into that. But since he was replaced, as far as I know, at some point in time can you tell us what kind of an officer he was as chief of SUP, what was he like?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: It's a bit uncomfortable to talk about a person who is not here, but since I took an oath to tell the truth I have nothing else that I can do but give you my perception of Mr. Cvetic as my first, immediate superior in Kosovska Mitrovica. One of the reasons why I was sent to Kosovska Mitrovica is this person called Cvetic who did -- who was not in charge of the situation on the ground in the territory of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP. He enclosed himself in the premises, in several rooms of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP. He hid there from his officers, avoiding to carry out his duties. And after going to meetings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, we have all this in the statement. Mr. Fila must be wanting more information or different information. Perhaps you could focus it better, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could you then tell us what kind of a man he was?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: If I could choose, I would never select him as my superior or my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So to cut the story short, he was a bad superior officer and as a person he was even worse than that, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I had for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fila. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How long do you envisage?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Less than one hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hopefully significantly less. We'll leave it to you to do your best. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogunovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My name is Djuro Cepic, as you have heard, I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Lazarevic. I will try to focus on specific questions, and therefore would you please take your statement. I'm interested in paragraphs 10 and 11.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Cepic repeat the paragraphs, we may have misheard him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you see this in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You see that there were joint actions of the MUP and the police, you also mention that in paragraph 12. I'm interested whether you were a member of the command structure or a member of the PJP units.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I was not a member of a PJP unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would I be right in saying that you did not see the plans for joint actions of the MUP and the army?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I did not see the plans for actions, either those of the MUP or those of the army, since MUP made exclusively plans for erecting obstacles and so on --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. So you didn't see any plans for joint actions?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now in paragraph 8 of your statement you say that in the territory of Kosovska Mitrovica SUP there were the 35th and 85th Detachment. Could we see document 5D1417 in e-court, please. While we're waiting for the document to come up, was Colonel Branko Prljevic the commander of the 35th Detachment, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, he was a classmate of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. He has also completed the military academy, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see the document here, we see the document of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we agreed that this -- that this document should be either replaced or not used because of this handwriting on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's your recollection, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: With your leave, we already have in the system a copy of this document without those handwritings on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So can we find it? Ah, there we are. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we have the other copies withdrawn or are they to remain there, Mr. Haider?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogunovic, secretariat in Mitrovica, 35th and 85th Detachment, are these the detachments that we mentioned?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. The next question has to do --

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, if I may explain. This document is something that I haven't seen before. I see it for the first time --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, I just wanted to ask you whether it was these units in that area.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I see that it says the 35th and so on -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see the 35th and the 85th Detachment, these are the detachments that were in the territory of Mitrovica, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogunovic, the 21st paragraph of your statement, RPOs. Could we see 4D521, please, in the meantime. While we're waiting for the document to come up, tell us this: You probably knew that a number of members of the RPOs came from the reserve military units. You knew that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see the document now. It is from the summer of 1998, and in this document the military district command addresses the MUP of Serbia due to a problem whereby military conscripts were assigned to the RPO units without there being a prior consent from the military. Were you familiar with this problem?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't, since I spent very little time working in this area, in Kosovska Mitrovica, and at this time I was in Djakovica where there were very few RPOs, if I'm not mistaken just seven of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have a document here from the wartime confirming the existence of RPOs during the war, and in order to speed this up would you agree with me that it is possible that RPOs existed during wartime without you knowing about it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: During the war, as far as I know, reserve police squads were disbanded, reserve policemen became members of the police force, whereas military conscripts went to their assignments in units according to their wartime assignments. It is possible that there was an individual or two that remained, but they were neither members of the MUP or the army or any other formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I suppose that you didn't have insight into the entire area of Kosovo and Metohija, but rather just the territory of your own SUP?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Since I'm under oath I can speak only about those things that I know of and things that happened where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we see 6D802. Mr. Bogunovic, these are conclusions from the meetings of the 7th and 11th of May, 1999, of the MUP of Serbia and could we see item 19, please. Could you please read item 19, please.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see it. The letters are too small.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: They will zoom in now.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: "Members of the RPO may not wear police and military uniforms if they have not been mobilised and engaged in reserve formations of the MUP and the Army of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you personally receive conclusions from these meetings?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I do not receive conclusions. It is the person who attends the meetings that receives conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Oh, all right. Thank you. Would you please look at paragraph 56 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do, paragraph 19 there suggests that you're wrong about the reserve police squads. What do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say that reserve police squads were disbanded and that they did not exist at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But this document indicates that they did exist; how could that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not attend the meeting. As far as I know in the territory of Kosovska Mitrovica police squads were disbanded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that the extent of your knowledge, confined to Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can only speak about places where I was. At that time I was in the territory of Kosovska Mitrovica, and it is my position that police RPOs did not exist, that the members who had been activated --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, paragraph 56 of your statement, would you please take a look at that. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I have carefully looked at the document that you refer to and I see that it has to do with the accused person Sasa Radojcic due to murder of a member of the Army of Yugoslavia. You probably know, or rather, do you know that these proceedings were further dealt with by the military judiciary?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: As for this, I can only say that I always had good cooperation with members of the army and that there were exchanges of information going both ways and that we did everything in accordance with the law as far as the prosecution, or rather, the implementation of any case we were working on was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This was murder, it was a Serb killing a Serb if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, Your Honours, in the document, 5D955, this incident is described under number 1, the one that was just referred to. [In English] P955, not 5D, page number 13 in e-court system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The transcript's not recording the number you gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I will repeat. P955, page 13 in e-court system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogunovic, you said that exchanges of information went both ways. I'm going to show you a document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please call up in e-court 5D991, please, the 13th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the last paragraph of this document, the 180th Detachment of the military territorial defence in the territory of Kosovska Mitrovica. We see down here that arrest was carried out and -- of a civilian who was engaged in arson, who was setting houses on fire, and that he be handed over to MUP organs.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: As for this particular case, I knew about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Were there other such cases when the army would arrest some civilians and they would catch committing a crime and then hand them over to you and then you would deal with them?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I said a few moments ago that I had an exceptionally good cooperation with the members of the Army of Yugoslavia. As for all information we had regarding any crime regarding any crime that took place in my area, we exchanged information on that and we took appropriate measures. I in my own chain and the gentlemen from the military in their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this a suitable time to interrupt you, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, we have to have a break at this stage for 20 minutes. While we have that break, could you please leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We shall resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogunovic, in your statement in paragraph 67 you refer to the Bajgora action. I would be interested in what preceded that action. Was this area a powerful terrorist stronghold and did terrorists often attack from that area?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Our intelligence was - and we exchanged that intelligence with the army - that this was one of the major KLA strongholds in the area of Kosovska Mitrovica along with a few others that I wouldn't want to refer to now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is one of them the area of Drenica or Srbica?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In that area, before the bombing started, were there frequent terrorist attacks in February/March 1999?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think that in my statement I did say that, that this was a hotbed and the MUP practically never went there. It was only after the activities carried out by the MUP and the army, and very briefly at that, and it was afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In a few documents you described that in late April and in May there was fighting in that area with the terrorist forces. This fighting involved independent operations on the part of the army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that all these military documents that you refer to in your statement were documents that you first saw during your proofing, right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I first saw them when General Lukic's Defence showed them to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 83, the on-site investigation in the village of Izbica. This on-site investigation was carried out by a team from the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: The on-site investigation was carried out on the basis of an order issued by the judge of the district court of Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You personally did not attend, am I right if I say that, you were not at the on-site investigation yourself?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: You are right. In addition to the persons mentioned here, my immediate superior was there, the chief of the secretariat, Vucina Janicijevic, he was on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that with regard to the investigation and with regard to the autopsy that followed, all of this was done at the request of the investigating judge of the district court in Kosovska Mitrovica and the district public attorney?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: We do that only in accordance with instructions issued by the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Here in the lower part of this paragraph you say that experts from the military medical academy carried out the external examinations and exhumations. You must have misspoken because exhumations are carried out by the court and examinations can be carried out by anyone, military doctors or a doctor from any civilian institution.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I see that it is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: These experts from the VMA, they work on orders from the district court, right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: The court was looking for the right people to do that and that's what they found.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogunovic, paragraph 89 of your statement, check-points. You probably know that military organs at their separate check-points and at mixed check-points were only in charge of the members of the Army of Yugoslavia, whereas the members of the MUP at their own check-points and at mixed check-points were in charge of all other persons?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: That is why there were these joint check-points, so as to have clear-cut authority. The MUP is in charge of civilians and everyone, and the army is in charge of people in uniform from the Army of Yugoslavia or Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that moment it was the Army of Yugoslavia; it became the Army of Serbia later?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Lieutenant-Colonel Dikovic, that was his rank at the time, this is paragraph 90, his criticism of military check-points. A document is referred to here, one of his documents. In all fairness, it's a document from the corps and you said that you did not see that. Do you know that Colonel Dikovic in that period of time, that is to say in April/May 1999, was in the area of Glogovac?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: As for Mr. Dikovic, Lieutenant-Colonel Dikovic, I know him personally. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, something went wrong, right? At that time I assume that he was in the territory of my municipality because it borders on Glogovac and that is the municipality of Srbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Petar Damjanac from the Glogovac SUP testified here and he confirmed that Colonel Dikovic was in his territory, the territory of the SUP of Glogovac.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: He personally, that is possible, but I assume that part of his unit was in my area too.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If he were to address anyone it would be logical for him to address your colleagues at the Glogovac SUP, right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one correction, it's not SUP Glogovac, it's OUP --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- and it's different capabilities of OUPs and SUPs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Under which SUP was the OUP of Glogovac? Let's clarify that.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The SUP of Pristina then?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 91 of your statement, Mr. Bogunovic, you say that members of the VJ were in towns and you mention those towns. Do you know whether the forces of the Pristina Corps -- well, you were in Kosovska Mitrovica, weren't you, and they left the barracks in Kosovska Mitrovica and the town itself before the bombing started and they took up areas of deployment outside built-up areas?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I know that the barracks in Mitrovica was evacuated by the military and the police, or rather, that they vacated the premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And you probably know that these military forces left the town together with materiel and equipment for the most part?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'd rather not discuss issues that I'm not hundred per cent certain of because I'm under oath and I don't want to say something that wouldn't be truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These uniformed persons that you saw in town, or rather, in towns you mostly saw people moving about unarmed mostly going from their units home or back to their units?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can say that I'm a person who spent a lot of time out there in the territory because the first person in our SUP didn't do that himself, and while doing so I met a lot of persons wearing the Army of Yugoslavia uniforms. In most cases those were old uniforms. It's either uniforms known under number 57 or 75, I'm not sure, and that there were fewer camouflage military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you perhaps know that these old uniforms that you mentioned were mostly worn by the members of civilian defence?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 92 of your statement. Could we now see 6D1027, please. You stated here that there were some attempts to implement resubordination, that that did not occur, you mentioned Colonel Savic. We will now take a look at one of his documents. Could we see the second page of the said document. You see that this is dated 3rd of June, 1999?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is his attempt to issue tasks to the MUP forces and it remained at the level of an attempt; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: As for Colonel Savic, I can say that I had frequent contact with him, and I were to choose the person I would like to work with it would be him. As for this document, I have never seen it and I talked to him about resubordination. Since I wasn't competent to decide on this and since I am not the kind of person who exclusively dealt with actions, and as far as I can remember that was the sole reason for resubordination and the tasks that I performed within the ministry, they were identical both in peacetime and in wartime, which means that those were issuing of passports, ensuring law and order, apprehending perpetrators of crimes, and other tasks as specified by law.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At any rate, there was no resubordination to Colonel Savic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP is concerned, there was none.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have just mentioned to us the tasks that you performed in peacetime and in wartime. You will agree with me that in wartime in Kosovska Mitrovica there were no Crisis Staffs, that the courts, the prosecutor's office, and the municipality operated normally just like all other civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: As for the secretariat where I was, we followed routine principles and regulations in force at the time. As for the Crisis Staff, I heard that term somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But there was none in practice?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: All I can say about that is that the equipment and materiel that we came across out there in the field, we turned it over to the municipality and its services. Now, I can't really tell you anything about anything else because I'm not certain of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So to conclude, the court, the prosecutor's office, civilian prosecutor, that is, and the municipality functioned during wartime?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In what context did you hear reference to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not from that area and I didn't know people from Kosovska Mitrovica or Djakovica, so I mostly dealt on -- dealt with the issues within the secretariat, people who hailed from these OUPs and police stations, the local ones, they maintained contact with people from the local self government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me ask you the question again in case you didn't understand it. In what context did you hear reference to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The body that is charged with taking over property from citizens that remained unclaimed or unprotected. It was in that context that I heard of it. Representatives of the local government, inspection services, and so on were involved in these issues in other organs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So do we take it from that answer that there was a Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can't claim that because I'm not 100 per cent certain and I would rather not say anything that I'm not 100 per cent certain of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who spoke of it to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard that when talking to my subordinates, when property items were turned over, and I mentioned that in the written statement given to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you help me with that, Mr. Cepic, where is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's paragraph 93 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's staff not Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed, we're talking about Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Maybe I made a mistake with my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You got the answer from him that he had heard reference to a Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Maybe it was in my question, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, his answer was: "As for the secretariat where I was, we followed routine principles and regulations in force at the time. As for the Crisis Staff, I heard that term somewhere," and I just want to know where he heard it, but it's become a bit more complex than that because it looks as though there might have been one. So it's -- it would be helpful to know a little more about the context in which it was referred -- it was mentioned to him. You've told us that subordinates talked about the Crisis Staff when property items were turned over. Were they turning over property to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, was that question directed to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogunovic, I'm a bit confused now because you say Crisis Staff now and in your statement it says just staff.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: A slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So what do you have in mind, just the staff or the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And a bit earlier you told me that all structures functioned, that is to say the municipality, the court, the prosecutor's office, the inspection services?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: According to the regulation in force at the time, this SUP was not duty-bound to take care of the property --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you about this. You said that all kinds of authorities in town functioned.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And we can see it in the document?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see in the statement that you mentioned the staff and now you told us the Crisis Staff. Do you have any direct knowledge of it, did you ever go there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I never went to any staffs, and I have already explained that. As for the Crisis Staff, people from the prosecutor's office, judiciary, were not members of that staff, people from the municipality were, people who dealt with inspection services, all kinds of inspection services. I don't want to enumerate all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So it was exclusively people who were employed in the Kosovska Mitrovica municipality?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 96 of your statement you speak of the Kosovska Mitrovica municipality and its territory, and then you mention 5D985. You explained the situation with the wounded members of the army in the Bair region.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 5D985, please. Could we have the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We can see now in the middle of the page the description of the event. You will agree with me, won't you, that these soldiers who were injured were at that point in time on duty securing the military warehouse in the Bair facility?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with me since I know that part of the barracks, that is to say warehouses where ammunition was stored, are located there. I know that the army held that part under its control.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to cover something else very briefly. Mr. Bogunovic, who was the chief of the secretariat in Pec, do you remember that by any chance?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: It was Mr. -- I know him but the name escapes me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can I say that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was it Vojislav -- Borislav Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know Blagoje Djordjevic from the Pec SUP?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I've heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. You started telling us something and then I asked you about the preceding paragraphs about planning of activities and you spoke about erecting barricades, raids, and so on, and other activities of the SUP. So now let us look at the plan so that we can see what those activities looked like in the Pec SUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 5D1422.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object at this point. Mr. Paponjak was here testifying about the area of SUP Pec. I don't know why should this witness testify about Pec municipality when he emphasized several times that he's testifying only about events in his municipality, so Djakovica and Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, what knowledge does this witness have of events in Pec?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not speaking about direct knowledge in the Pec municipality. It's just that the witness when prompted by me said that the SUPs normally planned the erection of barricades and raids, so I was interested whether indeed it was the case in the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP where this witness worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, he's told you that but --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could I discuss it with him on the basis of this document? I just need to put two questions to him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If necessary, Your Honours, I can explain to you how SUPs work. The SUP where I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, just let us determine what to do about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's a risk of the position in Pec being misunderstood should this evidence be presented in the light of a document which has no bearing on the area with which this witness is familiar, Kosovska Mitrovica. So if you want to ask questions, ask them directly of the witness, but please do not refer to circumstances in Pec. In your submissions if you see a similarity, you can no doubt draw our attention to that similarity.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogunovic, if the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP were to find it necessary to conduct a blockade and a search in its territory, then that would need to be done in writing, correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Everything that is done in the Ministry of the Interior must leave a trace, which means that it has to be in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This plan of blockade and search in writing should contain the place of commission, the time of commission, the objective, the way in which this was carried out, material and technical resources, equipment and weapons for the execution of the task, the preparation for the execution, and ultimately information and reporting as well as a recapitulation of the manpower and equipment used. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: With regard to every activity, a plan should contain all the things that you referred to and other things that I would like to add because this was not complete. A plan of activities that would be carried out by a member of the Ministry of the Interior that I was in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: I point out, though, that this is a plan of activities, a plan of activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, what is that? Because we've just heard a lot of evidence from the last witness about things that were done without any trace being kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have one in my hands, Your Honour, so I wanted to show that to the witness to ask him whether that was the form that they used at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can ask the witness to describe what his plan of activities was. What the plan in Pec was, bearing in mind what the last witness has told us about the situation in the MUP staff, may be completely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave I would like to show the witness this document, and then he can say whether they worked differently in Kosovska Mitrovica at that SUP as compared to the Pec SUP. Perhaps we would gain time in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, we have decided that matter, Mr. Cepic. I think you have run your course. I think we should bring your cross-examination to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogunovic, who is it that drafts this plan within the secretariats itself?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: It depends on the activity that is supposed to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: For what activities to you plan these actions and activities?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA BOGUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if I were to speak about this it would take a while, searching apartments, catching perpetrators, and so on and so forth. Let us not tire the honourable Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
